author: Lesson, 1826
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수십 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 매우 드물게 한반도를 지나가는 나그네새로, 해안 모래사장, 사구, 하구, 삼각주 등에 찾아온다. 작은 무리나 큰 무리를 짓거나 다른 물떼새 무리에 섞여, 몸을 위아래로 흔들며 걷거나 달리면서 먹이를 찾는다. 곤충과 작은 게 같은 동물성 먹이를 먹는다. 번식지에서는 호숫가 모래땅, 사막, 자갈 섞인 땅의 잔돌 사이에 접시 모양 둥지를 틀고 한배에 알 3개를 낳는다.

art.subject: Greater Sand Plover (Charadrius leschenaultii), adult male in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean beaches on spring passage (April–May): forehead white with a black bar above it; a black mask through the lores, eye and ear-coverts; crown sides, hindcrown and hindneck rusty-orange, the centre of the crown grey-brown; cheeks below the mask, chin and throat white; a fairly narrow rusty-orange band across the upper breast, usually without a black upper border; back, wings and tail grey-brown, the outer tail feathers white-edged; belly, flanks and undertail white. Long, heavy black bill; dark eye; legs olive to greenish-grey.
art.pose: walking on sand with a bobbing motion, searching for food
art.scene: Korean coastal sandy beach and low dunes near a river mouth in spring (May), bright light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding, side view standing on sand: white forehead with a black bar above, black mask through the eye, rusty-orange crown sides and hindneck, white throat, narrow rusty breast band, grey-brown upperparts, white underparts, long heavy black bill, long olive legs

adult male breeding, head detail: white forehead with a black frontal bar, grey-brown crown centre bordered rusty-orange, black mask through the lores and ear-coverts, white cheeks and throat, heavy black bill
art.build: Medium-sized plover, about 21cm long, a little smaller than Pacific Golden Plover and clearly larger than Lesser Sand Plover; large, angular head and long-legged stance. Bill black, heavy and long for a plover, about as long as the head, with a bulging, pointed tip. Legs relatively long with the tibia clearly visible; the toes project beyond the tail tip in flight. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight a clear white wing-bar and grey-brown rump and tail with white sides. Runs, stops and tilts forward to pick prey.
avoid: Do not paint a short, blunt bill and short dark legs — that is Lesser Sand Plover (Charadrius mongolus).
Do not paint a black breast band or a black collar (Little Ringed Plover, Kentish Plover).
Do not paint a white face without a black mask and a broad chestnut band edged black below — that is Oriental Plover.
Do not paint yellow or orange legs.
